invsbw.desc: A short hunting bow: a single stave of weathered brown wood whose two limbs mirror each other around a leather-wrapped grip exactly at the middle, both limb tips ending in identical pale horn nocks, and a thick pale tan twine bowstring clearly visible running straight from tip to tip, so the bow is shaped like a capital letter D. Shown upright, side view.
invsbw.note: the sample round's sbw words (round 2, approved)

invhbw.desc: A hunter's bow made from a single crooked branch: the two limbs are not smooth arcs but wander in three or four gentle, irregular bends along their length like a knotty stick, the bark stripped to weathered grey-brown wood with dark knots and two or three short stubs of trimmed twigs, a grip of rawhide strips wound round the middle, both tips cut into simple notches and bound with dark sinew, a thin pale twine string running perfectly straight from tip to tip and nothing else crossing the bow. A D whose curved side wobbles like a crooked stick, not a smooth curve. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left, the bow arching to the right.
invhbw.shape: crooked-bow: short-bow's D whose limbs wobble in three irregular waves each, the two limbs out of phase; a short grip block at the middle; the string straight on the left
invhbw.note: our 猎弓 line (Hunter's / Razor / Blade Bow): the line's defining part is a stave cut from a crooked branch; own design: grey-brown stripped wood, twig stubs, rawhide grip (review round 1: the two-tone flat bow did not read as this line)

invcbw.desc: A composite horse-archer's bow of horn, wood and sinew: short limbs covered in dark brown birch bark, a slim leather-wrapped grip at the middle, and at each end a stiff straight ear of pale horn that bends sharply forward, away from the string, with a small bone string bridge at the bend; the string runs straight between the two bridges and along the ears to their tips. A recurve with angled ears, not a plain D. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left.
invcbw.shape: static recurve: a short D from a middle grip on the right to two bridges on the string line, then at each end a stiff straight ear (a seventh of the height) angled back out to the right, away from the string; the string straight between the bridges and along the ears
invcbw.note: our 复合弓 line (Composite / Double / Great Bow): own design, the eared steppe bow

invsbb.desc: A short battle bow whose two limbs are faced with broad flat plates of dark ox horn, blackish brown with streaks of translucent amber, each plate as wide as three fingers beside the grip and narrowing to a point near the tip like a long leaf, fixed to the wooden core with two small iron rivets; a thick grip of dark leather bound with iron wire between the two plates; short bare wooden tips bound with sinew, curving slightly forward away from the string; a straight pale string. A D with broad blade-like limbs, clearly wider than a plain stave. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left, the bow arching to the right.
invsbb.shape: plated-bow: short-bow's D with each limb a broad flat plate tapering to a point three quarters of the way out, then a thin bare tip turning a little right; the string straight on the left
invsbb.note: our 短战弓 line (Short Battle / Short Siege / Diamond Bow): the line's defining part is broad horn-faced limbs; own design: dark ox horn with amber streaks, riveted, an iron-wire grip (review round 1: the double-curved B outline was not this line's)

invswb.desc: A heavy short war bow: a straight rigid middle section of thick dark oak, a third of its length, with a small arrow shelf carved into it and leather wrapped round the grip, and from each end of it a thinner limb of pale ash backed with dark sinew, bound with cord at the joint, curving back toward the string to horn nocks; a thick twisted string. Straight in the middle and curved only at the ends, unlike a plain D. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left.
invswb.shape: riser bow: a thick straight vertical riser on the right, a third of the height, with a small notch for the shelf; from its ends two curved limbs bending left to the string's ends; the string a straight line on the left
invswb.note: our 短战争弓 line (Short War / Rune / Ward Bow): own design; the war bows share the straight riser (invlwb tall)

invlbw.desc: A tall longbow cut from a single stave of yew: a simple D of even curve, the limbs thick and rounded at the middle and tapering evenly to slim tips capped with small horn nocks, a narrow grip whipped with linen cord and no leather, knots and grain lines in the wood, a thin straight pale string from tip to tip. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left, the bow arching to the right.
invlbw.shape: long-bow: short-bow's D on the 2x4 canvas, filling its height, a shallow arc (depth about a fifth of the height), thin limbs, small nocks, the string straight on the left
invlbw.note: our 长弓 line (Long / Cedar / Shadow Bow): own design, the plain tall stave

invlbb.desc: A tall long battle bow whose two long limbs are faced with broad flat plates of dark ox horn, blackish brown with streaks of translucent amber, each plate as wide as three fingers beside the grip and narrowing to a point two thirds of the way to the tip, fixed to the wooden core with small iron rivets; a long grip of dark leather bound with iron wire; long bare wooden tips bound with sinew, curving slightly forward away from the string; a straight pale string. A tall D with broad blade-like limbs, clearly wider than a plain stave. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left, the bow arching to the right.
invlbb.shape: the plated bow on the 2x4 canvas: a tall shallow D, broad plates tapering two thirds of the way out, long thin tips turning a little right; the string straight on the left
invlbb.note: our 长战弓 line (Long Battle / Large Siege / Crusader Bow): invsbb's horn-plated limbs made long (review round 1: the B outline went with invsbb's)

invlwb.desc: A tall heavy long war bow: a straight rigid middle section of thick dark oak, a quarter of its length, with an arrow shelf carved into it and leather wrapped round the grip; from each end of it a long thinner limb of pale ash backed with dark sinew, bound with cord at the joint, curving back toward the string to horn nocks; a thick twisted string. Straight in the middle and curved only at the ends. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left.
invlwb.shape: the short war bow's riser bow on the 2x4 canvas: a thick straight riser on the right a quarter of the height, long curved limbs to the string's ends, the string straight on the left
invlwb.note: our 长战争弓 line (Long War / Gothic / Hydra Bow): own design, invswb's outline made long

invam1.desc: A huntress's stag bow, tall and slender: a single stave of weathered grey-brown ash in a gentle curve, its tips turning slightly forward, each tip capped with a short forked tine of pale stag antler that holds the string, the grip wrapped in spotted deer hide with the hair still on, two small barred feathers hanging from a thong below the grip, a thin straight string. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left.
invam1.shape: stag-bow: a tall slim D like the long bow whose tips turn slightly right and end in small two-pronged forks; a short thong with two feathers hanging below the grip
invam1.note: our 猎鹿弓 line (the huntress's Stag / Ashwood / Matriarchal Bow): own design, antler-tine tips and deer hide

invam2.desc: A huntress's tall recurve bow: from the grip each limb sweeps out in a deep curve and then, in its last fifth, bends back the other way, away from the string, so both ends recurve like the crest of a wave and the string lies along each recurved end before it reaches the tip; the limbs broad near the grip and slimming toward the ends, of amber-brown horn laminated over pale wood with a thin dark seam between them; small carved bone caps on the tips; a carved wooden grip wrapped in braided cord with a small leather arrow pad. A recurved outline whose ends flick outward, not a plain D. Shown upright, side view, the string on the left, the bow arching to the right.
invam2.shape: recurve-bow: a tall deep D with broad limbs whose last fifth reverses so each tip points out to the right; the string straight between the reversal points, then along the recurved ends
invam2.note: our 双曲弓 line (the huntress's Reflex / Ceremonial / Grand Matron Bow): the line's defining part is recurved ends on broad limbs; own design: amber horn on pale wood, bone tip caps, a braided grip (review round 1: reflex-bow's tips curled toward the string into rings and the bow read as a plain D)

invlxb.desc: A light hunting crossbow seen from directly above, lying flat: a slim straight tiller of pale wood tapering toward a narrow butt, no shoulder stock and no pistol grip; across its front end a thin prod of horn and wood lashed to the tiller with cord, its two tips curving forward; no stirrup; the string drawn back to a small round nut a third of the way down the tiller, forming a V that points toward the butt; a short iron trigger lever under the rear half. The prod at the top, the butt at the bottom.
invlxb.shape: light-crossbow: the crossbow guide with the tiller half as thick and tapering to the butt, a thinner, wider prod whose tips curl forward (up), no stirrup ring, the same V string to a nut, a short lever
invlxb.note: our 轻弩 line (Light Crossbow / Arbalest / Pellet Bow): own design, slim with a lashed horn prod and no stirrup

invmxb.desc: A heavy medieval crossbow seen from directly above, lying flat: a straight narrow rectangular wooden tiller of even width with a plain square butt end, no shoulder stock and no pistol grip; a short thick steel prod crossing the front end like the bar of a letter T; an iron stirrup loop at the very front tip; the string pulled back from the prod tips to a round nut a third of the way down the tiller, forming a V that points toward the butt; a long thin iron lever along the rear half. The prod at the top, the butt at the bottom.
invmxb.note: the sample round's mxb words (round 2, approved: style A s202)

invhxb.desc: A heavy siege crossbow seen from directly above, lying flat: a broad thick wooden tiller bound with iron bands, a plain square butt, no shoulder stock; across the front a short massive steel prod lashed to the tiller with thick cord bindings; a big iron stirrup at the very front tip; the thick string pulled back to a heavy nut, forming a V that points toward the butt; and at the butt a winding crank: a toothed iron rack running along the tiller to a small iron gear box with an L-shaped crank handle sticking out to one side. The prod at the top, the butt at the bottom.
invhxb.shape: heavy-crossbow: the crossbow guide on the 2x4 canvas with the tiller twice as thick, a short thick prod, a large stirrup ring, the V string; a thin rack line down the tiller to a square gear box near the butt with an L handle sticking out right
invhxb.note: our 重弩 line (Heavy Crossbow / Ballista / Colossus Crossbow): own design, told from the crossbow by its bulk and the rack-and-crank at the butt

invrxb.desc: A repeating crossbow seen from above, tilted a little so the right side of its magazine shows: a straight wooden tiller with a plain square butt, a short prod of wood and horn across its front end, and riding on top of the tiller's front half a long narrow wooden box magazine bound with iron straps, the fletched ends of a few bolts showing in the slot along its top; the string runs back from the prod tips into a notch in the magazine; a long wooden lever joined by an iron pin to the magazine's rear runs back beside the tiller to a pivot near the butt. The prod at the top, the butt at the bottom.
invrxb.shape: repeating-crossbow: the crossbow guide without the stirrup, a long rectangular box over the tiller's front half (its right side face a thin strip), a slot line along its top, the V string ending at the box's front, a long thin lever beside the tiller on the right from the box's rear to near the butt
invrxb.note: our 连击弩 line (Repeating Crossbow / Chu-Ko-Nu / Demon Crossbow): own design; the box magazine and its lever make it

invgpl.desc: A throwing flask of foul gas: a small gourd-shaped bottle of thick greenish glass, two round bulbs with the lower one larger, filled with murky bilious green liquid full of small bubbles, a thin scum of yellow-green on its surface, a cork stopper sealed under a scrap of leather tied round the neck with twine. Shown upright.
invgpl.note: Rancid Gas Potion (gps, our 恶臭毒气药水; D2's file names run opposite to the codes): the gas line's smallest, a gourd bottle shared in shape with the oil potion

invgpm.desc: A throwing flask of choking gas: a pear-shaped glass bottle with a long narrow neck, wrapped in a net of knotted brown cord, filled with cloudy poison-green liquid that glows faintly from within, dark wax poured thick over the cork and running down the neck. Shown upright.
invgpm.note: Choking Gas Potion (gpm, our 窒息毒气药水): a netted pear bottle, shared in shape with the exploding potion

invgps.desc: A heavy gas bomb: a round glass globe filled with thick swirling poison-green liquid glowing from within, held in a cage of riveted iron straps that cross over it, an iron cap on top with a small ring. Shown upright.
invgps.note: Strangling Gas Potion (gpl, our 呛息毒气药水): the gas line's largest, an iron-caged globe, shared in shape with the fulminating potion

invopl.desc: A fire bottle for throwing: a small round-bellied flask of thick clear glass with a short neck, filled to the shoulder with pale golden lamp oil, light straw-yellow like clear cooking oil, never red or brown; a thick twist of oily grey rag stuffed into the neck as a wick, a tuft of it sticking up above the neck and a frayed tail hanging down one side of the flask, tied round the neck with twine. Shown upright.
invopl.note: Oil Potion (ops, our 火油药水): the fire line's smallest, the same round flask as invgpl's pick with a rag wick; the oil must read yellow, apart from the scarlet healing flasks (review round 1: dark amber came out red-brown and read as a healing potion at 34 px)

invopm.desc: A fire bomb: a pear-shaped glass bottle with a long narrow neck, wrapped in a net of knotted brown cord, filled with glowing orange liquid like molten embers, a short twisted fuse cord sticking up out of a wax plug in the neck. Shown upright.
invopm.note: Exploding Potion (opm, our 爆炸药水): a netted pear bottle with a fuse

invops.desc: A heavy fire bomb: a round glass globe filled with bright churning orange-yellow liquid glowing from within like a furnace, held in a cage of riveted iron straps that cross over it, an iron cap on top with a short fuse cord. Shown upright.
invops.note: Fulminating Potion (opl, our 爆燃药水): the fire line's largest, an iron-caged globe with a fuse

invqvr.desc: A quiver of arrows: a tall round quiver of stiff brown leather on a wooden base, a tooled band around its mouth and another around its foot, a leather carrying strap fastened down one side with iron rings, and a bundle of about a dozen arrows standing in it, their shafts and fletchings sticking out of the top, grey goose feathers and russet barred feathers. Shown upright, the open end at the top.
invqvr.note: our 箭矢 (Arrows): own design, feathers up, told from the bolts by the round tube

invcqv.desc: A bolt case for crossbow bolts: a straight-sided square box of dark stained oak boards, open at the top and as wide at the bottom as at the mouth, its four corners bound with riveted iron angle straps and a broad iron band round the mouth, a leather carrying strap hanging in a loop from two iron rings on one side; standing in it about a dozen short thick crossbow bolts point up, each with a heavy dark iron head shaped like a small four-sided pyramid with a flared collar at the shaft, the heads sharp-edged and clearly pointed, not rounded; no fur, no hair, no hide. Shown upright, front view, the open end at the top.
invcqv.shape: bolt-case: a straight-sided box, not tapered, banded at the mouth, a staggered row of short pointed bolt heads above it
invcqv.note: our 弩矢 (Bolts): own design, an iron-bound oak case with the heads up, told from the round leather arrow quiver (review round 1: the tapered hairy-hide quiver was too near the original's design and its heads read as pencils)
